name: UNH Thompson School Sawmill
use: Teaching sawmill for Thompson School forest technology students; mills lumber harvested from university land
builtText: 1968 (pole barn built by UNH faculty and students)

renovations.what: Fund-raising campaign ($230,000 goal plus $100,000 UNH match) for a band saw, heated classroom, upgraded electric service and running water

facts.text: The sawmill is a 45-by-100-foot pole barn built by UNH faculty and students in 1968 on Mast Road.
It has served UNH since 1968 for research, education and sustainable lumber production; all lumber is harvested from university land by Thompson School forest technology students.
In 2006 the mill, with its handset carriage and circular saw, was described as increasingly obsolete, and a campaign was raised to renovate it.
The site connects directly to College Woods and has parking, water, power and year-round educational facilities.
The Forestry FACTS plan would expand the site around the sawmill with a maple-sugaring operation, Christmas-tree research and demonstration areas, with Phase 1 targeted for fall 2026.

verdict: A 1968 pole barn built by faculty and students, now a timber-trussed teaching mill cutting lumber from university woods.
notes: Whether the 2006 renovation was completed isn't directly confirmed. The 2018 and 2021 COLSA reference photos show a modern band-saw line (not the old circular saw), which suggests it was. Interior per references: big open timber-truss shed with a translucent ridge strip and warm wood; rustic but handsome and functional. A search snippet attributed a 1960 construction date to UNH Magazine, but the article I opened says 1968. No licensed photos; no reviews.
judgeNotes: Reference photos show a warm, handsome timber shed with a modern band-saw line.
